references.text: Earlier in the chapter, the south side of the courtyard is described with its hundred cubits, providing context for the total measurements mentioned in verse 18.
Describes the actual construction of the courtyard with the same dimensions: a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide.
Repeats the same measurements for the courtyard and mentions the twisted fine linen (שֵׁשׁ מָשְׁזָר) used in the hangings.
Mentions the same material, finely twisted linen (שֵׁשׁ מָשְׁזָר), used for the tabernacle's tent coverings.
Notes the bronze sockets (אַדְנֵיהֶם נְחֹשֶׁת) for the pillars, the same material mentioned in verse 18.
Solomon's temple also had specific dimensions, showing continuity in God's detailed instructions for holy buildings.
Ezekiel's temple vision also includes a courtyard with specific measurements, linking it to the tabernacle's courtyard.
Highlights the connection between God's instruction and its fulfillment in history.
